subject.title: Gateway memory growth due to repeated file read errors

question: Should this be fixed as a scheduled memory/CORE.md producer bug, a generic read-tool directory behavior change, or folded into the broader gateway memory-leak investigation?
rationale: Source inspection supports partial fixes and one remaining failure shape, but the right owner boundary depends on whether the bad paths are producer bugs or an intended read-tool contract change.

options.title: Reproduce and fix producer path
options.body: Run a current-main gateway scheduler reproduction with heap/RSS diagnostics, then fix the scheduled producer or retention path that emits memory-system/CORE.md and directory reads.

options.title: Change read-directory semantics
options.body: Teach the generic read tool to return a directory listing only if maintainers accept the model-facing tool contract change and add compatibility coverage.

options.title: Track under broader gateway leak work
options.body: Treat this as adjacent to the gateway memory-leak cluster if live diagnostics show the read failures are incidental rather than causal.

recommendation.title: Reproduce and fix producer path
recommendation.body: Run a current-main gateway scheduler reproduction with heap/RSS diagnostics, then fix the scheduled producer or retention path that emits memory-system/CORE.md and directory reads.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent history touches both the generic read tool and heartbeat scheduler, the two unresolved boundaries that need maintainer direction.
